note: D2 provisions nothing and migrates nothing, so most upstream NFRx.y are application-level with no infrastructure expression and are recorded N/A with the reason rather than claimed as covered. The OK rows are the ones infrastructure or the pipeline genuinely carries: the test targets, the per-screen check, the one metric, and NFR14.30 - which appears as an OK row precisely because what monitoring carries for it is the explicit statement that NOTHING can observe it. NFR14.15 and NFR21.1 are citations of prior rules, not IDs defined here. The reverse array lists D1 requirements this unit CITES rather than owns, including three that are cited specifically to record that they do NOT apply to a unit with no migration - which is worth stating, because 'does not apply to D2' is not 'closed'.
